pairs.subject: accessibility
pairs.evidence: desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:661 The phone's problem selector exposes only pointer activation, leaving keyboard users without an equivalent selection path on this surface.

techniques.evidence: tools/phone-panel-test.cjs:888 The test claims reader output from a source-attribute assertion; it does not observe announcement delivery, timing, or repeated messages.
desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:528 Inactive panels are conditionally unmounted; Paper's draft state lives in the parent, preserving it without leaving inactive controls mounted.
desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:661 Problem selection uses a nonfocusable div with a pointer handler and no keyboard equivalent in the Point & ask panel.

desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:737 The persistent region renders one state string directly, without a drain queue or deliberate repeat mutation, so bursts can overwrite messages and identical consecutive refusals produce no new mutation.
desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:678 The rewrite textarea has neither an associated label nor an explicit accessible name; the nearby heading and instructions are not wired to it.
desk/src/app/globals.css:57 Join refusal triggers this nonessential shake without reduced-motion handling; the imported reduced-motion rules target other selectors and do not suppress it.
desk/src/app/phone/ExplainTalk.tsx:36 The reusable recording control is a focusable native button whose behavior is wired exclusively to pointer events, so keyboard activation does nothing.
